name: A repository names its language servers in a committed file
summary: A checkout's committed .archboard/language-servers.json names its language servers, and a global file fills the rest, so a repository that installs its servers through nix, devenv or devbox needs no setup on each machine or in CI.

changes.value: repo list, add, use, forget and language-server: the checkouts bindings resolve to, the chosen one for each repository, and the language servers that a repository or this machine names

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/XppR9owz#jAKtfzMA
changes.value: Keeps this machine's checkout registry. repo add registers a checkout, with the worktrees git lists for it, or an untracked vault, and never changes which checkout of a repository is chosen. A checkout whose identity is an untracked vault's name keeps it, and the answer's renamed gives the vault's new name. repo use chooses one. repo forget removes one; list shows each, chosen or gone. None of them calls a server: every running server watches the registry file. language-server, in language-server.ts beside it, shows, sets and removes the servers of the working directory's checkout in its committed .archboard/language-servers.json, of the chosen checkout that --repo names, or of this machine with --global; the registry holds no servers.

value.label: show and write a repository's or this machine's servers

value.name: Language server files
value.responsibility: Reads and writes the language servers that a checkout's committed .archboard/language-servers.json and the global language-servers.json name, the repository's first
value.description: TASK-599 and ADR 0046. A repository names its servers in a file that it commits, so every machine and CI run that has the checkout runs the same ones, with no trust step. The global file sits beside the registry and fills each language that the repository file leaves out. A relative command in the repository file is a path from the checkout root, so a repository can commit a wrapper script. A file that cannot be read decides every language that it could name. A write keeps the languages in a fixed order and deletes a file that names no server.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/6E6hL0Zk#1aoB46lM
changes.value: TASK-367.13 to TASK-367.16, TASK-433, TASK-599 and ADR 0046. One pass starts the server of each language once per project on its first question: the checkout, for Swift the package that holds the file, for C, C++ and Objective-C the directory of its compile_commands.json. It speaks JSON-RPC over the child's stdio, asks textDocument/definition at the last name of a use on its line, and textDocument/documentSymbol once per file to tell code that runs from a member of a type. A language's row in languages.ts says what its server needs beyond that: pyright is told the checkout's .venv or venv; csharp-ls the solution nearest the root; sourcekit-lsp starts normally, builds and prepares its Swift package through background indexing, is asked workspace/synchronize with index true once and has each file opened; clangd has each file opened, finds its compile_commands.json where it would, keeps its own index where an editor's clangd does, and is asked once that index has ended. The command comes from Language server choice. Every language but TypeScript runs only what the checkout's committed .archboard/language-servers.json names, else the global language-servers.json beside the registry, with the environment of the Archboard server and nothing added; if neither names one, or a file cannot be read, the pass says so once for the checkout and the language, naming the command that writes one. TypeScript runs what the choice names: the native tsc --lsp of the checkout's TypeScript 7 or later, typescript-language-server for an earlier TypeScript, and in a checkout of Archboard its own tsc otherwise. Every server has stopped before the pass returns: shutdown and exit, then a kill of its process group, or a kill at once when the pass is cancelled. A server that fails is said once for its checkout, and so is a project it cannot answer about, for which no server starts: a C file with no compile_commands.json.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#FMiMVZ28
changes.value: A server that the checkout's language server files name wins and runs as an editor's would. A file that cannot be read gives its problem instead. TypeScript has a default that reads the checkout's own node_modules/typescript at its root. Version 7 or later runs its native tsc --lsp --stdio. An earlier version, which has no --lsp, runs typescript-language-server from the checkout's node_modules/.bin or the server's PATH, told to use the checkout's lib/tsserver.js. Without either, a checkout of Archboard falls back to Archboard's own native tsc, and a release, which ships no TypeScript, reports the server as missing and says why. The TypeScript that the choice read is reported with the check's timings.
